span.label: what the COVID-19 pandemic did to the mental health of undergraduates at one large university, asked in a semistructured interview a month after the state stay-at-home order
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: which pandemic stressors students report, how severely each affects them, and why so few used the counselling service available to them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an interview survey of undergraduates during the pandemic peak, carrying both a literature-derived twelve-category severity rating and an open thematic coding of the same transcripts
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: student distress during a pandemic, recorded through two instruments at once - one whose categories were fixed by earlier papers and one with no categories at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: semistructured Zoom interviews by 20 trained undergraduate researchers, transcribed by an AI service and manually verified, with PSS-10 scores, a four-point severity rating over twelve categories, and open thematic coding by a single coder reviewed by two others
span.term: semistructured Zoom interviews by 20 trained undergraduate researchers, transcribed by an AI service and manually verified, with PSS-10 scores, a four-point severity rating over twelve categories, and open thematic coding by a single coder reviewed by two others
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same interviews are read twice - once against twelve categories written by earlier papers and rated 0 to 3, once with no categories at all. Whatever the open coding surfaces that the twelve do not contain is a direct measurement of what the literature's vocabulary could not see. THE COMPARISON IS AVAILABLE IN THIS PAPER AND IS NOT DRAWN
span.term: two apertures on one set of transcripts
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: open coding without a priori codes means the themes are whatever a trained reader sees. One person did all of it; two others were brought in afterwards to resolve discrepancies and discuss saturation. That is a review, not an independent coding, and no agreement statistic is available because none could be computed
span.term: the coder is the instrument, and there was one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the interviews were run by 20 trained undergraduate researchers and none of the authors conducted one. That removes the authors' expectations from the elicitation and introduces twenty different interviewing styles into it - a trade the design makes deliberately and the paper reports plainly
span.term: twenty interviewers, none of them the authors
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: recordings were transcribed by an AI service and verified for accuracy manually. The qualitative data is therefore a machine's reading of speech, corrected - and what a correction pass catches is a different set from what it misses
span.term: a transcript produced by a machine and checked by hand
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: participants were also asked to describe stressors, coping strategies and barriers in a typical semester WITHOUT associating them with the pandemic. The within-person baseline is collected from the same person in the same sitting, which controls for who is answering and not for when they are answering
span.term: a non-pandemic comparison inside the same interview
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
